meta.title: San Diego — A Private Travel Itinerary

cover.duration_label: Five Nights · Four Days to Roam

summary.intro: This is a base-and-spoke trip, not a road trip. Seascape Sur in Solana Beach anchors all five nights and the days radiate out from it: north up Historic Highway 101 to a bluff at Swami's, south into the city for a farmers market, murals on freeway pylons, and a park built for a world's fair. Four narrow windows shape it — a late Thursday dinner, a Friday that ends at the airport, a Saturday that stops at three, and a Monday that runs to a red-eye.

rows.label: In
rows.value: UA1626, Wed Oct 7, into Terminal 2. Reconfirm on united.com — this flight number rotates routes.

rows.label: Out
rows.value: UA1827, Mon Oct 12, SAN 10:20 PM → Newark 6:37 AM. Terminal 2, 737 MAX 8.

rows.label: Bag drop
rows.value: United takes checked bags from about 6:20 PM. There is no luggage storage at SAN.

rows.label: Airport run
rows.value: 22 miles, about 26 min from the rental off-peak.

rows.label: Seascape Sur
rows.value: 521 S Sierra Ave, Solana Beach 92075. Gated, bluff-top, five nights.

rows.label: Beach access
rows.value: Use Fletcher Cove, 10 min north — it has a paved ramp and handrails. The complex's own access is stairs.

rows.label: On foot
rows.value: Seven Seas Roasting 13 min · Culture Brewing 16 · COASTER station 18 · Pizza Port 20.

rows.label: Northward
rows.value: Encinitas 10 min · Carlsbad 15 · Oceanside 22.

rows.label: Southward
rows.value: Torrey Pines Extension 8 min · La Jolla 24 · Balboa Park 25 · Little Italy 28.

rows.label: The car
rows.value: Yours every day, so every drive below assumes it.

rows.label: Rush hour
rows.value: I-5 at Sorrento Valley is a standstill 4–6:30 PM. Head north before 3 or after 7.

rows.label: Saturday parking
rows.value: 610 W Ash St garage, $5 all day at weekends. Street meters are enforced Saturdays.

rows.label: Balboa Park
rows.value: Now paid. Lower Inspiration Point gives the first three hours free.

rows.label: If you're drinking
rows.value: COASTER from Solana Beach to downtown in 36 min; station parking free. Sparse at weekends — check PRONTO.

rows.label: Valle
rows.value: Tock, immediately. Wednesday to Sunday only, so Sunday is the one night.

rows.label: Buona Forchetta
rows.value: OpenTable, Encinitas, for Friday dinner — it gets slammed.

rows.label: Il Fornaio
rows.value: Thursday, 8:15 PM. The kitchen runs to 9:30.

rows.label: Officine Buona Forchetta
rows.value: Monday dinner at Liberty Station. Open to 9 on Mondays.

rows.label: Anything physical
rows.value: Book refundable so it can be dropped on the morning at no cost.

rows.label: Torrey Pines
rows.value: Upper reserve closed for construction until March 2027. The Extension is open.

rows.label: Mondays
rows.value: Wayfarer, the Encinitas gardens and most Balboa Park museums are shut.

rows.label: La Jolla
rows.value: Art & Wine Festival closes Girard Ave Sat and Sun. Use Bird Rock and the Shores.

rows.label: Rail alerts
rows.value: Only matters if you switch to the train, but NCTD suspends coastal rail on ad-hoc weekends.

rows.label: Reconfirm
rows.value: Hours and closures verified October 2026. Check again in the week before you fly.

timeline.title: UA1626 into Terminal 2
timeline.body: Collect the car and head north — twenty-two miles, about twenty-six minutes to Seascape Sur. Worth reconfirming the arrival time against your booking: this flight number rotates between Newark, Charlotte and Orlando origins, and the published times differ by hours.

timeline.title: Working, then committed until eight
timeline.body: Nothing is scheduled around you. If a gap opens in daylight, Fletcher Cove is a ten-minute walk north and has a paved ramp down to the sand with handrails — no stairs, unlike your own complex's access.

timeline.title: Dinner in Del Mar
timeline.body: Il Fornaio, eight minutes south on Camino Del Mar. Ocean-view patio with the fires lit, and the kitchen runs to 9:30 — the only comfortable late table near your base on a Thursday.

timeline.title: Pizza Port, twenty minutes' walk
timeline.body: If you get out nearer eight. Brewpub, communal tables, their own beer, and the garlic-veggie pie. It closes at nine on Thursdays, so this is the quick version, not the leisurely one.

where_to_eat.note: 1555 Camino Del Mar. Housemade pasta, wood-fired pizza, the vegan cavolfiori. Kitchen to 9:30.
135 N Hwy 101, about a mile. Closes 9 on Thursdays.
Sixteen minutes on foot, on the Cedros strip. To 10 on Thursdays.

worth_knowing.blurb: Solana Beach's original beach access was blasted through the bluff by hand in the 1920s — locals called it the Tunnel, and it was the only way down to the sand for decades. The city has since replaced the scramble with a paved ramp and handrails, which is why it is the one stretch of this coastline you can reach without negotiating a staircase.

days.title: Highway 101, Northward
days.subtitle: Friday · Solana Beach → Encinitas → the airport

timeline.title: Coffee on Cedros, on foot
timeline.body: Seven Seas Roasting at 312 S Cedros is a thirteen-minute walk from the door — single-origin pour-overs and a soft-serve affogato. The design district around it is flat and good for an hour. Leave the car where it is.

timeline.title: Torrey Pines Extension
timeline.body: Optional and easy. A separate park unit from the closed main reserve, eight minutes south, free street parking on Del Mar Scenic Parkway. Take the Mar Scenic Trail and turn back whenever. If the back says no, Fletcher Cove and the ramp are two minutes from your door.

timeline.title: Prager Brothers, Encinitas
timeline.body: Naturally leavened bread and a properly laminated croissant on Coast Highway 101. They close at five, so this is the hard edge of the afternoon.

timeline.title: Swami's bluff
timeline.body: Golden hour opens at 5:50, sunset is 6:23, and the light holds until about 6:48. The whole afternoon has been drifting north up the old coast road to arrive here.

timeline.title: Dinner, five minutes away
timeline.body: Buona Forchetta's wood-fired Neapolitan on Coast Highway 101. Reserve on OpenTable — it gets slammed on a Friday and serves until ten.

timeline.title: The airport run
timeline.body: Encinitas to SAN is about forty minutes against no traffic at that hour. A late arrival means you can take dinner at its own pace rather than watching the clock.

where_to_eat.note: 312 S Cedros Ave. Veteran-owned micro-roaster, and a walk rather than a drive.
543 S Coast Hwy 101. Naturally leavened. Closes at five.
250 N Coast Hwy 101. Neapolitan, wood-fired, reserve ahead.

worth_knowing.blurb: Pinus torreyana is the rarest pine in North America, growing wild in only two places on earth: this stretch of coastal bluff and Santa Rosa Island offshore. The gnarled, wind-thrown shapes come from a tree trying to live in sandstone with almost no fresh water.

The surf break takes its name from the Self-Realization Fellowship on the bluff above it, founded by Paramahansa Yogananda in 1937. Its gold lotus towers are the landmark surfers line up against, and the collision of surf culture and spiritualism on one headland is about as San Diego as the city gets.

days.title: The City, and Back by Three
days.subtitle: Saturday · Little Italy & Barrio Logan

timeline.title: South, before the traffic
timeline.body: Twenty-eight minutes down the I-5 on a Saturday morning. Park at the 610 W Ash Street garage — five dollars all day at weekends, which is the single best parking fact in this document.

timeline.title: Little Italy Mercato
timeline.body: Six blocks of West Date Street, eight until two, the largest farmers market in the county. Breakfast here and eat properly. The Piazza della Famiglia and its three-tier fountain sit at the centre of it — a 16mm frame if ever there was one.

timeline.title: Chicano Park, Barrio Logan
timeline.body: Ten minutes south. The murals climb the Coronado Bridge pylons on flat ground, in deep shade under the freeway — this is where a fast 28-70 earns its place. The 16mm from the base looking up; the 70-200 for individual panels.

timeline.title: Café Moto and the museum
timeline.body: 2619 National Avenue, a solar-powered roastery running continuously since 1990. It shuts at 2:30 on Saturdays. The Chicano Park Museum on National Ave runs 11 to 5 and is back on the table now you are driving.

timeline.title: North again
timeline.body: Home by two, with an hour in hand before three. Going by train would have worked too, but the northbound gap between 12:49 and 14:09 made it a gamble against your cut-off.

where_to_eat.note: Eat properly here. Barrio Logan's vegetarian options thinned out when Border X closed.
2619 National Ave. Solar roastery, going since 1990. Closes 2:30 Saturday.
Paper-thin Milanese pizza if the afternoon frees up on the way home. Open to 10.

worth_knowing.blurb: In 1970, after a promised park under the new bridge turned out to be destined for a highway patrol station, residents occupied the ground and held it for twelve days. They won. The murals painted on the pylons afterwards are now the largest collection of Chicano art anywhere in the world, and the park is a National Historic Landmark.

days.title: Bread, Architecture, and Baja
days.subtitle: Sunday · La Jolla → Balboa Park → Oceanside

timeline.title: Wayfarer and Bird Rock
timeline.body: 5525 and 5627 La Jolla Boulevard, two doors apart, twenty-four minutes south. Wayfarer's founder was lead bread baker at Tartine in San Francisco; Bird Rock has been named Roaster of the Year. Go before 10:30 — the pastry sells out. Bird Rock sits south of the village, so the Art & Wine Festival never touches it.

timeline.title: Birch Aquarium at Scripps
timeline.body: 2300 Expedition Way, on the bluff above La Jolla Shores. Free three-hour parking, effectively single level, benches throughout, a hands-on tidepool exhibit and a terrace looking straight out to sea.

timeline.title: The Shores, on foot
timeline.body: Hard-packed sand, no steps, as far as suits you. If the morning is a good one this is where a snorkel would start — booked refundable, decided today, not last month.

timeline.title: Balboa Park
timeline.body: Park at Lower Inspiration Point: the first three hours are free, which is exactly this visit. Spanish Village and the Botanical Building both close at four, so take them first. The lath dome wants the 16mm, pointed straight up.

timeline.title: The organ concert
timeline.body: Free, one hour, seated, outdoors, five thousand pipes. Afterwards the Lily Pond, Casa del Prado and the Cabrillo Bridge, none of which close.

timeline.title: North to Oceanside
timeline.body: Forty-five minutes up the coast, and conveniently away from the Sunday evening traffic building around Petco Park downtown.

timeline.title: Valle
timeline.body: Mission Pacific Hotel, overlooking the pier. The Vegetariano tasting menu, and sunset at 6:21 arrives in the middle of dinner. Twenty-two minutes home afterwards.

where_to_eat.note: 5525 La Jolla Blvd. Strawberry-pistachio and almond are the ones. Closed Mondays; sells out by 10:30.
5627 La Jolla Blvd, two doors along. Farm-direct single origins; the city's benchmark roaster.
One Michelin star. The Vegetariano tasting menu, around $180. Wednesday to Sunday only — book on Tock.

worth_knowing.blurb: The Spanish Colonial Revival ensemble was raised for the 1915 Panama–California Exposition, largely to Bertram Goodhue's designs, and most of it was meant to be temporary. San Diego liked it far too much to pull it down. The Botanical Building at its heart reopened in December 2024 after a three-year, $28.5 million restoration.

days.title: Soft Landing
days.subtitle: Monday · checkout at ten, wheels up at 10:20

timeline.title: Check out, then coffee in Encinitas
timeline.body: Bags go in the car — that is what makes today work. San Diego airport has no luggage storage and United will not take a checked bag until about 6:20 PM. Then Ironsmith and Prager Brothers, 458 and 543 South Coast Highway 101: small-batch roasting, and the croissant you would have had at Wayfarer if it opened on Mondays.

timeline.title: San Elijo Lagoon
timeline.body: 2710 Manchester Avenue, Cardiff, nine minutes away. Flat boardwalks, free parking, nature centre nine to five. The gentlest thing on this itinerary and none the worse for it.

timeline.title: Lunch in Encinitas
timeline.body: Lotus Cafe is entirely vegetarian and open on Mondays, which narrows the field considerably on a day when half the county's best kitchens are dark.

timeline.title: Mount Soledad
timeline.body: Free, open to ten, and you drive to the top — no walking at all. A true 360 over the ocean, downtown, Coronado and, in October's Santa Ana clarity, well into Mexico. The best return on effort available today.

timeline.title: Liberty Station
timeline.body: The old Naval Training Center, flat throughout. Coffee, a slow wander, somewhere to sit before the light turns.

timeline.title: Sunset Cliffs
timeline.body: Arrive early — the lots fill three-quarters of an hour before sunset. Twenty yards from the car to the edge, and stay well back from it: a section near the Arch gave way in April. Sunset 6:20, light until 6:44.

timeline.title: Dinner, then Terminal 2
timeline.body: Officine Buona Forchetta at Liberty Station, ten minutes back, open to nine on Mondays. Away by 8:30 and at the airport by 8:45 — an hour and a half before UA1827, with a real meal behind you rather than a terminal sandwich.

where_to_eat.note: 458 S Coast Hwy 101. Small-batch, award-winning, and open on a Monday.
765 S Coast Hwy 101. Entirely vegetarian or veganisable. Andy's Swami's Lasagna.
2865 Sims Rd. Wood-fired, open Mondays to nine, ten minutes from Terminal 2.

worth_knowing.blurb: The Pleistocene sandstone along this headland erodes quickly, which is what carves the arches and sea caves below — and also why the edge is never quite where it appears to be. The bluffs are still actively failing: a section near the Arch gave way in April 2026.

packing.heading: What to Bring

items.label: A sling or a proper pack
items.body: An R6 and two zooms on a single shoulder strap is a real load across a day, and this whole itinerary is built around a back that is still healing.

items.label: The 16mm, specifically
items.body: For the Botanical Building's lath dome and the foot of the Chicano Park pylons — the two frames a 28mm simply cannot tell.

items.label: Layers for wind, not for weather
items.body: Seventy-five degrees on land and considerably less on a bluff at dusk. October is peak Santa Ana season, which can also mean ninety for a day.

items.label: Non-slip closed shoes
items.body: For wet sandstone at Sunset Cliffs and the tidepool edges, where the footing is the entire risk.

items.label: The PRONTO app, loaded
items.body: Buy the COASTER day pass before Saturday. You must tap at a platform validator before boarding — a cash fare earns no transfers.

items.label: Refundable bookings
items.body: Anything physical, the snorkel above all, booked so it can be dropped on the morning at no cost.
